sections.text: Critics of standardised testing frequently argue that it narrows the curriculum. The charge is not without merit, yet it tends to conflate the test with the uses to which it is put. A test designed to diagnose weaknesses may be entirely benign; it is when results are tied to school funding that teaching to the test becomes a rational, if regrettable, strategy.
